title: Priestly Conduct and Offerings

questions.question: If a priest is unclean, when can he eat of the holy things?
options: After he has bathed his body in water and the sun is down
questions.correctAnswer: After he has bathed his body in water and the sun is down
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:6-7 (ESV): "Shall wash his body in water. And when the sun is down he shall be clean; and afterward he may eat."

questions.question: Who else in the priest's house could eat of the holy things?
options: A slave purchased with his money or born in his house
questions.correctAnswer: A slave purchased with his money or born in his house
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:11 (ESV): "But if a priest buys a slave as his property for money, the slave may eat of it, and anyone born in his house..."

questions.question: Could a priest's daughter married to a stranger eat of the holy contributions?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:12 (ESV): "If a priest's daughter marries a layman, she shall not eat of the contribution of the holy things."

questions.question: What quality must an animal have to be accepted as a burnt offering?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:19 (ESV): "To be accepted you shall offer a male without blemish."

questions.question: What happens if you offer a blind, disabled, or mutilated animal?
options: It is okay for the poor
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:20 (ESV): "For it will not be accepted for you."

questions.question: How old must an animal be before it can be offered?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:27 (ESV): "From the eighth day on it shall be acceptable as a food offering to the Lord."

questions.question: What commandment was given regarding a cow/ewe and its young?
options: Do not kill both in one day
questions.correctAnswer: Do not kill both in one day
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:28 (ESV): "You shall not kill both her and her young in one day."

questions.question: When must the sacrifice of thanksgiving be eaten?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:30 (ESV): "It shall be eaten on the same day; you shall leave none of it until morning."

questions.question: If a priest's daughter is widowed or divorced and returns to her father's house childless, can she eat?
options: Yes, she may eat of her father's food
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, she may eat of her father's food
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:13 (ESV): "And returns to her father's house... she may eat of her father's food."

questions.question: If a man eats of a holy thing by mistake, what must he do?
options: Add the fifth part to it and give the holy thing to the priest
questions.correctAnswer: Add the fifth part to it and give the holy thing to the priest
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:14 (ESV): "Then he shall add the fifth of its value to it and give the holy thing to the priest."

questions.question: What does "profane His holy name" mean in this context?
options: Disobeying the laws of offerings and holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Disobeying the laws of offerings and holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:32 (ESV): "And you shall not profane my holy name... So you shall keep my commandments."

questions.question: Could a foreigner offering a vow present an animal with a blemish?
options: No, no blemish allowed even from a foreigner
questions.correctAnswer: No, no blemish allowed even from a foreigner
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:25 (ESV): "Neither shall you offer... from the hand of a foreigner... because they have a blemish... they will not be accepted for you."

questions.question: Which animals mentioned could have a limb "too long or too short" for a freewill offering but not a vow?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:23 (ESV): "You may present... an ox or a lamb that has a part too long or too short for a freewill offering, but for a vow it cannot be accepted."

questions.question: What physical state made a priest unclean (leprosy, discharge, etc.)?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:4 (ESV): "None... who has a leprous disease or a discharge may eat of the holy things until he is clean."

questions.question: Why did God bring them out of Egypt according to the end of this chapter?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:33 (ESV): "Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God: I am the Lord."

key_verse_text: So you shall keep my commandments and do them: I am the Lord.
